record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: Prove a uniqueness theorem for maximal Cauchy hypersurfaces assuming only the dominant energy condition, rather than the timelike convergence condition or existence of a timelike Killing field.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a globally hyperbolic spacetime, i.e., a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian manifold admitting a Cauchy hypersurface. A spacelike Cauchy hypersurface $\Sigma \subset M$ is called maximal if its mean curvature with respect to the future-directed timelike unit normal vanishes identically. Assume that the stress-energy tensor $T_{ab}$ of $(M,g)$ (via the Einstein equations $G_{ab} = 8\pi T_{ab}$, or directly as a symmetric 2-tensor) satisfies the dominant energy condition: for every future-directed causal vector $v^a$, the vector $-T^a{}_b v^b$ is future-directed causal.

Prove (or disprove) the following uniqueness statement: under the dominant energy condition alone — without assuming the timelike convergence condition ($\mathrm{Ric}(v,v) \geq 0$ for all timelike $v$) and without assuming the existence of a timelike Killing vector field on $(M,g)$ — any two maximal Cauchy hypersurfaces in $(M,g)$ must coincide (or, more generally, characterize the situations in which uniqueness fails).
artifact.status_search_result: Classical uniqueness results for maximal Cauchy hypersurfaces (e.g., Brill–Flaherty, Marsden–Tipler) require the timelike convergence condition or a timelike Killing field. Recent work on initial data rigidity under the dominant energy condition (e.g., Hirsch–Kazaras–Khuri–Zhang and related results) addresses rigidity aspects of DEC, but a general uniqueness theorem for maximal Cauchy hypersurfaces under DEC alone does not appear to be established in the literature found. Status remains unclear.

status_evidence.title: Initial data rigidity implies spacetime rigidity
status_evidence.snippet: Initial data rigidity results under the dominant energy condition and their spacetime consequences.
status_evidence.claim: Recent progress on DEC-based rigidity, but not a general uniqueness of maximal Cauchy hypersurfaces under DEC alone.

status_evidence.title: Existence of CMC Cauchy surfaces and spacetime splitting
status_evidence.snippet: Existence and uniqueness results for CMC/maximal Cauchy surfaces under timelike convergence assumptions.
status_evidence.claim: Standard uniqueness theorems still rely on timelike convergence, not DEC alone.
